data.name: United Kingdom

sources.label: Freedom House: country electoral and political indicators, 2026 edition

legitimacy.summary:
Our assessment: United Kingdom has broadly credible and competitive national electoral institutions. The latest country indicators support meaningful voter choice, sound electoral rules and an opposition able to contest governing power. This is not a guarantee that every contest is flawless, nor a judgement about the popularity of any party.

Evidence baseline: Freedom in the World 2026, covering conditions in 2025. Our review date is not the date of an observer verdict on a later ballot; subsequent contests may require a separate assessment.

data.coverageNote: Official UK-wide House of Commons party results and seats are recorded here for the 2010, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2024 general elections.

data.notes: Final UK-wide results from the UK Parliament Election Results archive. Party votes and seats are transcribed for every registered party in the official table. The Independent and other non-party candidates row aggregates the remaining 564,042 valid votes and 6 elected MPs after accounting for the official party table and the separately recorded Commons Speaker. The Speaker is listed separately; the 650-seat total includes the Speaker. Sinn Féin MPs are included in seat totals although they do not take their seats. Shares are calculated from exact votes as a proportion of 28,809,340 valid votes; turnout is valid votes divided by the official electorate. Smaller parties with no reusable saved profile are still included with neutral display colours.
